en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fourth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether the Bodhi is the Buddha:
Is the Bodhi the Buddha? Yes.
When enlightenment has ceased, vanished, and subsided,
is one not an awakened one? One should not say so … [as before] … Is one an awakened one because of enlightenment?
“Yes.
“Is one called a Buddha by virtue of past enlightenment?
“One should not say so,” and so forth.
Is one called a Buddha because of past enlightenment?
Yes. Does one perform the task to be accomplished by that enlightenment? No.
It should not be said so … [as before] … Does one perform the task to be accomplished by that enlightenment? Yes.
Does one fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, and develop the path by means of that enlightenment?
One should not say so… [and so on]… Is one called “Awakened” (Buddha) because of enlightenment?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is one a Buddha before enlightenment has been attained?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Is one called a Buddha because of future enlightenment?
Yes. Does one perform the task to be accomplished by that enlightenment? Yes.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Does one perform the task to be accomplished by that enlightenment? Yes.
Does one fully understand suffering through that enlightenment … [and so on] … develop the path through that enlightenment?
One should not say so … [and so on] … Is the Buddha enlightened by means of present enlightenment, and does he perform the duties of an enlightened one through that enlightenment?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is one a Buddha by means of past enlightenment, and does one perform the task of enlightenment by means of that same enlightenment?
You must not say so… [and so on].
Is one awakened by means of present enlightenment; and by that enlightenment, does one fully understand suffering, abandon its origin, realize its cessation, and develop the path?
Yes. Is one awakened by means of past enlightenment; and by that enlightenment, does one fully understand suffering … [and so on] … develop the path?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one a Buddha by virtue of present enlightenment, and does one perform the task of enlightenment by means of that enlightenment? Yes.
Is one a Buddha by virtue of a future enlightenment, and does one perform the duties of enlightenment by means of that future enlightenment?
One should not say so... [etc. ...
Is one a Buddha by virtue of a present enlightenment, and does one fully understand suffering, [and so forth], and develop the path by means of that present enlightenment?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is one a Buddha with respect to a future enlightenment, and by means of that enlightenment does one fully understand suffering … [and so on] … develop the path?
You must not say so … [and so on].
Is one awakened by means of past enlightenment, yet does not perform the task of enlightenment by means of that past enlightenment?
Yes. Is one awakened by means of present enlightenment, yet does not perform the task of enlightenment by means of that present enlightenment? Yes.

It should not be said so … [as before] … Is one a Buddha by virtue of past enlightenment, yet does not through that past enlightenment fully understand suffering … [and so on] … develop the path? Yes.
If one is a Buddha by virtue of present enlightenment, does one not fully understand suffering through that enlightenment … [and so on] … does one not develop the path?
One should not say this … [and so on].
If one is a Buddha by virtue of future enlightenment, does one not perform the duties of enlightenment through that enlightenment? One should not say this.
“Yes.
[The opponent asks: “Is one a Buddha by means of present enlightenment, yet does not perform the task of enlightenment by means of that enlightenment? [The respondent replies:
“One must certainly not say so…” [and so on].
Is one a Buddha by means of future enlightenment, yet does not, by that enlightenment, fully understand suffering … [and so on] … develop the path?
Yes. Is one a Buddha by means of present enlightenment, yet does not, by that enlightenment, fully understand suffering … [and so on] … develop the path? No.
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is one a Buddha by virtue of past enlightenment, a Buddha by virtue of future enlightenment, or a Buddha by virtue of present enlightenment?
Yes, one is.
Is one a Buddha by means of the three types of enlightenment?
One should not say so …pe… Is one a Buddha by means of the three types of enlightenment?
“Yes,” you say.
“Is it the case that one who is constantly, continuously, and uninterruptedly endowed with and established in the three forms of enlightenment has the three enlightenments present before him?
You should not say so… [and so on].
Is it not to be said that one is "awakened" by means of awakening?
Yes, it is.
Is it not the case that one is called a Buddha because of the attainment of enlightenment?
Yes, it is so.
If indeed one is a Buddha because of the attainment of enlightenment, then, verily, it must be said:
“Awakened by means of awakening (bodhi).
Is he called “awakened” because of the attainment of awakening? Yes, he is. Is he awakened by means of awakening?
Yes, he is.
Is awakening the attainment of awakening?
One should not say so... [and so forth].
The discussion on whether one is awakened by means of awakening is finished.
